title: Q-ASHBY-gating: keep one kept knob value per recurring situation
body:
**Owner:** operations
**Trigger:** executor tick, driver order
**Done check:** cmd:python3 -m foundation ashbymap --probe gating
**Status:** open

Problem: A knob holds one value. When the situation changes (the free-tier level the tick already reads goes from ok to lean or degraded and back), the value adapted to the old situation is overwritten by the search in the new one and must be found again on return. Ashby's journal (index: Gating, J.6165; Accumulation demands separate channels, J.6227; Ancillary regulations, J.5684, J.5777) says adaptations to situations that recur need separate channels.

Build: Add table `goal_knob_memory (knob_id, situation, value, kept_at)` to the DDL in `seed/worker/src/goals.js` and `export function gate(memory, situation)` to `seed/worker/src/ashby.js`. When a change is kept, store it under the current situation; when the situation changes and a kept value exists for the new one, restore it as a logged step that is reviewed like any other. The situation is the free-tier level from `seed/worker/src/freetier.js`. Tests in `seed/worker/test/ashby-loop.test.js`: adapt in A, adapt in B, return to A restores A's value in one step. Bind the concept `gating` in `doctrine/ashby-concepts.json`.

**Prediction:** ashby_gaps <= 3 within 720 h

**Out of scope:** learned situation classifiers; more than the three free-tier levels; tenant knobs (the tenant applies its own values).

size: M

**Closing probe:** `python3 -m foundation ashbymap --probe gating` passes when the concept is implemented and every mechanism it names exists (ASHBY-KERNEL-1).
